_doc: Rules that turn the ILSpy decompile of the game's car-driving code into the copy in JunctionRules/Vanilla/. tools/vanilla_copy.py applies them (generate) or proves the copy equals decompile + these rules (check). Every deviation must also be listed in DEVIATIONS.md under the same id.

files.original_type: Game.Simulation.CarNavigationSystem (incl. nested Actions, UpdateNavigationJob, UpdateLaneSignalsJob, UpdateLaneReservationsJob, TrafficAmbienceEffect, ApplyTrafficAmbienceJob, ApplyLaneEffectsJob, TypeHandle)

renames.reason: Own type name so the game's system and the copy can both exist in one World.
The copy's navigation job must call the copied iterator, not the game's.

namespace.reason: Copied types live in the mod's own namespace. Inside 'namespace Game.Simulation;' every type of Game.Simulation and of its parent Game was visible without a using; the two added usings restore exactly those lookups (a name that became ambiguous would be a compile error, never a silent rebind).

deviations.reason: ILSpy 8.2 prints the IL float negation 'neg' as '0f - x'. That is not the same operation: -(+0) is -0 but 0f - (+0) is +0, so the decompile changes the sign of zero results. Restores the game's unary minus. Verified by tools/IlHash --copy: all 33 sites are 'neg' in Game.dll and every one is followed by a primary expression, so '-x' parses exactly like the original.

marked_blocks._doc: Hand-written stage 2 code allowed only between '// JR-STAGE2 BEGIN <id>' and '// JR-STAGE2 END' lines; vanilla_copy.py check removes them and proves the rest equals decompile + rules. Each block is insert-only (no vanilla line inside is changed). Every id is described in DEVIATIONS.md (section S2).

S2-01.reason: Iterator field holding the car's stage 2 state (JRWholeJunction).

S2-02.reason: Both IterateFirstLane overloads: the lane checked next is the car's current lane; 0.2.3: remembers the current lane(s) (the car's own approach, never counted as a feeding lane).

S2-03.reason: IterateNextLane: the lanes checked from here are ahead of the current lane.

S2-04.reason: CheckOverlappingLanes, before the overlap loop: entry spot (red excluded, amber live; 0.2.3: no mid spots), where the car is, first uncrossed point of a junction (node) lane, and (0.2.3) the car's motion for the arrival time (lane drive speed from the stock speed limit and turn cap).

S2-05.reason: Per overlap: is it part of the whole-path decision (start at or after the waiting spot, yield-checked).

S2-06.reason: Blocking reservation: stop at the spot of its stretch; while crossing a safety stop before the first uncrossed point if the car can stop (0.2.1).

S2-07.reason: Car asking for space (priority 96): stop at the spot; dropped while crossing (0.2.1).

S2-08.reason: Pedestrian on a crossing of the path: distance swapped to the waiting spot before commit.

S2-08b.reason: Restores the game's distance after the pedestrian check.

S2-09.reason: Keeps the other car's position before the game's priority look-ahead.

S2-10.reason: While crossing with no safety stop possible the look-ahead is undone unless the other car is past the overlap start (game's own committed semantics); 0.2.3: deciding / safety re-check: the stock 2 s look-ahead becomes 2 s + the car's own arrival time.

S2-11.reason: Car on a conflicting lane: braking distance swapped to the waiting spot before commit (projected cars, crossings).

S2-11b.reason: Restores the game's distance after the vehicle check; counters.

S2-12.reason: 0.2.3 arrival-time projection: cars on the lanes feeding the conflicting junction lane, projected by the car's own arrival time, as virtual reservations through the unchanged stock reservation test (deciding / safety re-check only); 0.2.4: skips cars stopping at that lane's red / amber (the stock-read signal componentData2), scans only for the deciding car (not followers, not when already held or when the lane's own reservation holds it), per-car-update memo, bounded work.

S2-13.reason: 0.2.4 (owner ruling 14 Nov 2026, setting 'Turning across oncoming traffic gives way', whole junction only): after the stock num6 -= num9, a turn across the oncoming flow gets the lower priority against that oncoming straight when both have equal signs (no sign / signal override, no Stop / Yield / RightOfWay / Unsafe difference); the straight car is not held by the turner's reservation alone (S2-06).

S2-20.reason: Job fields: stage 2 mode, the debug counter array; 0.2.3: the safety-stop event table (debug) and a read-only ConnectedEdge buffer lookup (feeding lanes). 0.2.2's trailer lookups removed (no mid spots).

S2-21.reason: Hands the mode and the read-only lookups (0.2.3: Owner, Lane, SubLane, ConnectedEdge for the feeding lanes; the counter array) to each car's iterator.

S2-22.reason: Debug counters, once per car and step, only when counting (0.2.3: safety-stop events via the car's entity and the simulation frame).

S2-23.reason: OnUpdate: takes this step's mode from the main-thread handoff; 0.2.3: the safety-event table and the ConnectedEdge lookup (0.2.2 trailer lookups removed).
